subject.title: Windows: lstat bottleneck causes 2-3x slower performance vs Mac (59% of CPU time)

question: Should OpenClaw accept operation-scoped realpath caches inside plugin hook/skill and sandbox containment checks for this Windows lstat fix?
rationale: The proposed implementation is a narrower alternative to a process-wide cache, but it still changes cache lifetime around security-sensitive path containment and needs an explicit maintainer tradeoff decision.

options.title: Accept operation-scoped caches
options.body: Land the linked PR once exact-head checks remain green and maintainers accept one caller-owned cache per hook, skill, bind-validation, and sandbox path-resolution operation.

options.title: Limit optimization to non-boundary paths
options.body: Reject cache reuse in containment checks and keep Windows lstat work focused on plugin metadata and other non-security-boundary paths.

options.title: Pause for a formal cache contract
options.body: Hold the linked PR until maintainers define the exact allowed cache lifetime for plugin and sandbox realpath checks.

recommendation.title: Accept operation-scoped caches
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR once exact-head checks remain green and maintainers accept one caller-owned cache per hook, skill, bind-validation, and sandbox path-resolution operation.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned on the linked PR and recently owned the adjacent manifest-registry cache change on main.
